exact_question: For each of the four Q041 FULL/start0 configurations explicitly reconstructed in run 38140371059, what rigorously controlled bounds can be placed on the differences in the complete electron-fraction history x_e(z) and cumulative Thomson optical depth tau_T(z) between an event-resolved latch at q=xHeII=10^-6 and a reset to q=0 at the same first cutoff event, with identical captured effective inputs and fixed accepted z_reio?

continuation.background: Admitted primary guard row57, exact inherited E/Y/V_previous; E_input_left is conservative whole-cell energy cap; no scalar consumption.
continuation.selection: conv(HMLA,SWIFT) for each fixed q branch
continuation.hypothesis: An existing absolutely-continuous source-real solution satisfying the admitted background and fixed-q two-operator inclusion, starting from the inherited h and w face; no assumed future domain membership. The invariant bounds apply on its existing interval and at a1 whenever an admissible continuation reaches a1. Exact discontinuous-selector existence/uniqueness is not established.
continuation.proof: Until the first exit, positive atomic/source/C premises hold on the larger outer box. The decreasing positive Riccati comparison excludes lower-h exit. Strict upper-h and both thermal inward faces exclude all other exits. The bounds persist at the closed endpoint for existing admissible continuations. Convex combinations preserve these linear derivative inequalities.
